summary: A steel house on a concrete pier marking Milwaukee's harbor entrance, commissioned in 1927, manned until 1966; now privately owned and closed.

access.note: Offshore; reached only by boat; not open to the public.

events.note: Placed in commission 26 February 1927 per Lighthouse Service Bulletin; the nomination says established 1926
Lighthouse Service merged into the Coast Guard; Coast Guard personnel assigned as keepers
Head keeper Michael Rotta killed in a fall while painting the lighthouse (21 May 1952 per Lighthouse Friends)
Fourth-order Fresnel lens removed, replaced by a VRB-25 beacon
Declared excess by the Coast Guard, June 2011

notes_for_editor: Disagreements: built/established 1926 (nomination) vs commissioned 26 Feb 1927 (Bulletin, LF); Rotta's death 1952 (LF, Milwaukee Magazine) vs 1953 (OnMilwaukee); focal plane 61 ft vs 67 ft; foundation crib vs caissons. The record's Fl G 2.5s and first_lit 1899 look wrong (1899 is the earlier 'Milwaukee Breakwater Old' station; USLHS lists Emil C. Tews as its keeper 1899-1907 though the nomination calls that south-end light unmanned; not used). LF says the Army Corps owns the pier; the nomination says the USCG owned the lighthouse. The Rogan and Rotta family events, Eckert's 1955 duty, Schreiber's recollection and the 1928 Harbor Station rest on Lighthouse Friends (secondary; draws on Lighthouse Digest 2003), not checked against the original. Bulletin text is poor OCR; quotes copied as OCR'd. The 24 Coast Guard roster lines come from the USLHS roster only; Jack Eckert (1955) is named as LF names him but is not on the roster. The 2024 article was read as reproduced by News Pub (jsonline blocked). The Commissioner's 1927 report is not in the corpus (cited via LF). Chronicling America (WI) searches returned no hits. milwaukeebreakwaterlighthouse.org had a certificate error and was not read. focal_height_m 18.6 = 61 ft per nomination; height 16.2 m = 53 ft per USLHS. Bulletin page cited by PDF page 4 (found with corpus.py). No photos added.
